missing_states.description: No error.tsx at wiki route level. Errors during WikiLayoutContent or children components bubble up to the dashboard root error boundary or Next.js default. A wiki-specific error boundary would allow graceful degradation (e.g., 'Wiki unavailable — try again later' instead of crash).

No error.tsx at article route level. MDX compilation errors are caught internally (WikiArticleError), but data fetching errors (getCachedArticleAndNode, Promise.all for EI/sources/siblings) have no route-level error boundary. A database failure during the parallel data fan-out would crash the entire article page.

No not-found.tsx at [slug] level. When article is not found, notFound() throws to the nearest parent not-found boundary. Currently falls to the dashboard or root not-found page. A wiki-specific 404 with 'Article not found — browse the sidebar for available topics' would be better UX.

Client-side getTaxonomyTree() call in useEffect has no .catch() handler. If the server action throws, the Promise silently fails, leaving loading=true permanently. The sidebar shows the inline skeleton indefinitely.

Promise.all([getEIPromptsForArticle, getUserEIResponsesForArticle, getArticleSources, getRelatedTopics, getArticleSiblings]) has no individual error handling. A single rejection crashes the whole fan-out. In demo mode, these are skipped, but in live mode they're collectively fatal.
getBreadcrumbTrail and getCachedTaxonomyTreeFull have no try/catch. If either throws (DB connection issue, etc.), the entire WikiHeader crashes, taking down the breadcrumb bar and mobile navigation.

getCachedTaxonomyTreeFull uses unstable_cache with 2h TTL. If the cache is cold and the DB is down, this throws. There's no fallback to stale data or a graceful error UI within the sidebar Suspense boundary.

observations: All 21 wiki navigation/article/shared components have proper 'use client' or async server boundaries
Wiki content has 3-layer loading: (1) route-level loading.tsx, (2) WikiContentShell ArticleSkeleton for client transitions, (3) inner Suspense around WikiArticle MDX compilation
Demo mode skips personalization, sources, and siblings — enables fast rendering for smoke tests
Widget system is fully lazy — only loads JS for widgets present in article content
All robots metadata set to { index: false, follow: false } — no wiki content is indexed
Article metadata falls back gracefully through: explicit fields → node fields → computed defaults
Prev/Next navigation operates on taxonomy siblings, not article chronology
Empty states are well-handled for sources, related topics, ToC, bookmarks (return null)
Reading progress uses scroll container ref, not window — works correctly within the wiki center pane
Bookmarks use optimistic UI — updates local state immediately, rolls back on server error
